decisive_items: fetal MRI at 25 weeks, which showed a 2.3 cm porencephalic cyst in the right frontotemporal–insular region
Cranial ultrasound on day 1 showed a right porencephalic area
response.rationale: The vignette explicitly identifies a porencephalic cyst and porencephalic area on imaging, making porencephaly the most specific and directly supported diagnosis. Other findings like microcephaly and micropolygyria are features of the condition, while intracranial hemorrhage is a suggested antecedent but not the final diagnosis.

rejected.why: Maternal CMV serology is IgG positive/IgM negative and febrile episode is nonspecific; no direct evidence of congenital infection, and toxoplasma was negative.
Microcephaly is a clinical finding, not the underlying diagnosis; it is a symptom of the porencephalic condition.
Genetic disorder is unsupported because gene sequencing and metabolic screening were normal; microcephaly and micropurpura are not specific.
Micropolygyria is a localized cortical abnormality, not the overarching diagnosis; it is part of the porencephaly complex.
Intracranial hemorrhage was suggested on ultrasound but not confirmed on MRI; it is a proposed cause, not the final diagnosis.
